identification: Framed colour reproduction print of a Russell Drysdale painting of a seated woman in a straw hat with white collar and gloves, 50 x 40 cm, in a pale timber frame. It is a print, not an original. Backing carries an Italian-language Drysdale biography/caption slip and a J.M. & J.N. Cocker picture frame makers label (20 The Quadrant, Launceston, phone 2 2789). The specific painting title was not identified; the Italian caption refers to a Drysdale work called 'Donna di Campagna' (Country Woman), which may be this image.

Cocker, Picture Frame Manufacturers, 20 The Quadrant, Launceston'. No artist signature or edition number seen on the print front.

identification: Yamaha alto saxophone with brown hard case and a folding saxophone stand. Gold lacquered brass body, nickel-plated keys, mother-of-pearl key touches, Yamaha tuning-fork logo engraved on the neck (confirmed in a zoom of photo 3). The look (lacquered body, nickel keys, student build) is consistent with the Yamaha YAS-21 / YAS-23 / AS-100 type student altos, but the YAS model stamp and the serial number are NOT legible in any of the 5 photos (bell engraving in photo 4 is visible but too small and blurred to read; no photo shows the neck receiver or the body under the thumb hook). Model is therefore unconfirmed.
marks_seen: Yamaha tuning-fork logo on neck (photo 3 zoom). Engraving on bell near the bow is visible in photo 4 but illegible. No model stamp or serial number visible. Brown vinyl-covered hard case with chrome latches and a handle, with a lot tag. Mouthpiece with metal ligature and cork present. Folding chrome tripod stand.
google_searches: Not run for identification beyond the photos; Terapeak sold searches were used to match Yamaha student alto models by look.

viewing_check: Estimate 60-100, current bid $25. Must check at viewing: model stamp (YAS-21/23/25/26 or AS-100; value ranges from about $280 to $700 depending on model), serial number and country of manufacture (Japan), neck and body condition (dents, bent keys, leaking pads, cork), whether the neck fits and the case latches work. Case is old and scuffed. Sax case is large and posts at roughly A$60-100 interstate. Prices are mostly 1-2 years old and steady to slightly up for YAS-21 type altos. Model unconfirmed from photos.

flip_reason: 4 sales of the YAS-21 type at $283-$394 (typical about $330) in 2024-2026, plus AS-100 $363 and YAS-23 $456. Current bid is $25 (about $31 with premium) vs estimate 60-100. Profit could clear $200 if it is a YAS-21 or better and playable, but model is unconfirmed, postage is high and a sax needs a service, so it is not an easy flip.
